title: Finite test for supported homogeneous division
statement:
Let $D\subset\mathbf N^n$ satisfy $D+\mathbf N^n=D$ and be monotone, meaning $\alpha-\alpha_i e_i+\alpha_i e_j\in D$ whenever $\alpha\in D$ and $i<j$. List its finite vertices $\alpha_i$ in ascending degree-lexicographic order, put $d_i=|\alpha_i|$, and set $\Delta_i=\{\beta:\alpha_i+\beta\in(\alpha_i+\mathbf N^n)\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}(\alpha_j+\mathbf N^n)\}$. There is $b(D)\in\mathbf N$ such that the following holds over any commutative ring $A$. Here $A[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]$ is the subring of finite-support series in $A[[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and a series is homogeneous of degree $d$ when all its nonzero coefficients have total exponent degree $d$. For homogeneous polynomials $H_i\in A[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]$ of degrees $d_i$, let
$$\mathcal P_q=\{Y^\beta H_i:\beta\in\Delta_i,\ |\beta|+d_i=q\}\ \amalg\ \{Y^\gamma:\gamma\notin D,\ |\gamma|=q\}$$
be an indexed family. If $q\ge b(D)$ and $\mathcal P_q$ spans the homogeneous degree-$q$ module, then $\mathcal P_t$ spans it in every degree $t\ge q$. In each degree this family is a basis whenever it spans, so testing the finitely many degrees at most $b(D)$ suffices for unique homogeneous division in all degrees. This conclusion applies separately to every degree prefix of a monotone diagram, and to its restriction to the variables occurring in its vertices.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13, pp.93--94, referring to Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), 207--302; detailed input Theorem 8.1, Definition 8.3 and Remarks 8.4 (pp.273--275). No Stacks tag states this result; journal text read through the publisher-version PDF online, absent from the repository literature.

proof.text: For $n\ge1$ take $b=d+n(\max(1,d)-1)+1$, where $d=\max(\{0\}\cup\{d_i\})$. If $k\ge b$ and $\mathcal P_k$ spans, [lem-trf-supported-coordinate-face-lifting] gives the lifts $Q$ for every coordinate face into $S=\operatorname{Span}_A\mathcal P_{k+1}$. All its generators have degree $k+1$. Since $k+1>0$, [lem-trf-homogeneous-coordinate-lifting-criterion] gives $S=V_{k+1}$. This $b$ depends only on the diagram, not on $A$ or the forms.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Theorem 8.1 and its application in Theorem 9.6, pp.274--275 and 282; subarguments isolated as cited. Online PDF https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf

proof.text: Starting from the given $q\ge b$, induct on $t-q$: the base is the assumed spanning at $q$, and Step 1 applied at $k=t\ge b$ gives the successor. For $n=0$ choose $b=0$: the only nonzero homogeneous component is $V_0=A$, so spanning at $q$ propagates directly to all $t\ge q$.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Theorem 8.1 and its application in Theorem 9.6, pp.274--275 and 282; subarguments isolated as cited. Online PDF https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf

proof.text: In every degree, [lem-trf-supported-degree-coefficient-isomorphism] identifies the family indices with the finite monomial basis and shows that spanning makes its coefficient map bijective. Hence each spanning family is a basis. If every degree at most $b$ spans, Step 2 applied at $q=b$ gives spanning in all degrees. Its unique basis coefficients, grouped by vertex, are precisely the supported quotients and complementary remainder in [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Conversely unique division gives spanning in the test degrees. This also covers $n=0$.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Theorem 8.1 and its application in Theorem 9.6, pp.274--275 and 282; subarguments isolated as cited. Online PDF https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf

proof.text: By [lem-trf-monotone-prefix-essential-restriction], each degree prefix has exactly the retained ordered minimal vertices and unchanged quotient supports. Restricting either $D$ or a prefix to its own essential variables preserves monotonicity, ordered minimal vertices and degrees, with supports given by extension by zero. For each resulting diagram $D'$ let $n'$ be its number of variables and $d'=\max(\{0\}\cup\{|\alpha'_i|\})$. Relabel the variables increasingly and apply Steps 1--3 with $b'=d'+n'(\max(1,d')-1)+1$ if $n'>0$, and $b'=0$ if $n'=0$. The support identities identify the required indexed family exactly; all homogeneous forms over every commutative $A$ are allowed. Thus each prefix, restriction and prefix followed by restriction has its own bound independent of $A$ and the forms, as asserted. Empty prefixes and empty variable sets are included.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Theorem 8.1 and its application in Theorem 9.6, pp.274--275 and 282; subarguments isolated as cited. Online PDF https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf

lean.statement: theorem exists_finiteDivisionTest (n s : ℕ) (D : Set (Fin n →₀ ℕ)) (a : Fin s → Fin n →₀ ℕ) (hD : IsMonotone D) (ha : IsOrderedVertexFamily D a) : (∃ b : ℕ, ∀ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A), IsFiniteDivisionTest D a A b) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, ∃ b : ℕ, ∀ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A), IsFiniteDivisionTest (generated (prefixVertices a d)) (prefixVertices a d) A b) ∧ (∃ b : ℕ, ∀ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A), IsFiniteDivisionTest (generated (essentialVertices a)) (essentialVertices a) A b) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, ∃ b : ℕ, ∀ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A), IsFiniteDivisionTest (generated (essentialVertices (prefixVertices a d))) (essentialVertices (prefixVertices a d)) A b)
